title: Cross Product and Its Applications
topicTitle: Cross product (vector product) and its applications
notes: **Definition.** a × b = |a||b| sin θ n̂, where θ is the angle from a to b (0 ≤ θ ≤ π) and n̂ is the unit vector given by the right-hand rule, perpendicular to the plane of a and b.
**Determinant form.** a × b = (a₂b₃ − a₃b₂) i − (a₁b₃ − a₃b₁) j + (a₁b₂ − a₂b₁) k, equivalently the formal determinant with rows i, j, k; a; b.
**Anti-commutative.** b × a = −(a × b). Swapping the order reverses the direction while preserving magnitude, so the order must always be stated.
**Worked example.** a = (1, 2, 3), b = (4, 5, 6): a × b = (2·6 − 3·5, 3·4 − 1·6, 1·5 − 2·4) = (−3, 6, −3), and dotting with a gives −3 + 12 − 9 = 0, confirming perpendicularity.
**Parallel and perpendicular.** a × b = 0 iff a and b are parallel (or one is zero); for perpendicular unit vectors |a × b| = 1, while i × j = k, j × k = i, k × i = j.
**Area.** The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides a, b is |a × b|; the area of triangle ABC is ½ |AB × AC|, which is zero exactly when A, B, C are collinear.
**Scalar triple product.** [a b c] = a · (b × c) is the (signed) volume of the parallelepiped on a, b, c; the tetrahedron's volume is one sixth of it.
**Coplanarity.** Three vectors are coplanar iff [a b c] = 0. This also gives the condition for four points A, B, C, D to be coplanar via AB, AC, AD.
**Moment of a force.** The moment (torque) of force F about a point O is M = r × F, where r runs from O to the point of application; |M| = |r||F| sin θ is the turning effect.
**Unit normal.** n̂ = (a × b)/|a × b| gives a unit normal to the plane containing a and b, used to write the plane's equation in vector form r · n̂ = d.
**Distributivity.** a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c and (k a) × b = k(a × b); the cross product is NOT associative, so a × (b × c) ≠ (a × b) × c in general.
**Vector triple product.** a × (b × c) = (a · c) b − (a · b) c, the 'BAC − CAB' identity; it is a vector lying in the plane of b and c.
**Exam caution.** a × b is a VECTOR, while a · b is a scalar; a mixed expression such as (a × b) · c is valid but a × (b · c) is not defined.
summary: The cross product a × b is a vector perpendicular to both a and b with magnitude |a||b| sin θ, equal to the area of the parallelogram they span. Its determinant form drives area, volume, moment and collinearity calculations throughout Class 11 vector algebra.
importantStatements: a × b is perpendicular to both a and b.
|a × b| equals the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b.
The scalar triple product vanishes if and only if the three vectors are coplanar.
importantNotes: The cross product is anti-commutative: b × a = −(a × b).
A zero cross product signals parallel vectors, not necessarily a zero vector.
examShortTricks: Compute a × b with the 3 × 3 determinant, then dot it with a and with b as a one-line accuracy check.
For triangle area use ½|AB × AC|; if the result is zero the three points are collinear.
Use |a × b| = |a||b| when the vectors are given perpendicular, avoiding component arithmetic.
formulas: a × b = (a₂b₃ − a₃b₂, a₃b₁ − a₁b₃, a₁b₂ − a₂b₁)
Area of parallelogram = |a × b|;  Area of triangle = ½|a × b|
[a b c] = a · (b × c);  Volume of parallelepiped = |[a b c]|
examples: Find the area of the triangle with vertices A(1, 0, 0), B(0, 1, 0), C(0, 0, 1). AB = (−1, 1, 0), AC = (−1, 0, 1); AB × AC = (1, 1, 1), so area = ½√3.
Find a unit vector perpendicular to both a = (1, 1, 0) and b = (0, 1, 1). a × b = (1, −1, 1), |a × b| = √3, so n̂ = (1, −1, 1)/√3.
practiceQuestions: Compute a × b for a = (2, −1, 3), b = (1, 4, −2) and verify it is perpendicular to both.
Find the area of the parallelogram with diagonals (3, 1, −1) and (1, −2, 1).
confusion: Treating the cross product as commutative; reversing the order negates the result.
Confusing |a × b| with a · b: the former uses sin θ and is an area, the latter uses cos θ and is a scalar projection.
practice: Compute three cross products and verify each with a dot-product check.
Derive the area of a triangle from a cross product for two different vertex orderings.
universalFacts: The cross product is defined for 3-D vectors (and as a scalar curl in 2-D).
|a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|² |b|² holds for all vectors a, b.
specialNotes: The direction of a × b follows the right-hand rule: curl the fingers from a to b, the thumb gives n̂.
A plane through a point p with direction vectors u and v has normal u × v and equation (r − p) · (u × v) = 0.
examNotes: Write the determinant expansion explicitly; sign errors on the j component are the most common loss of marks.
Include units for area and moment in applied problems.
importantTasks: Solve four area problems by cross product

mcs.explanation: sin 0° = 0, so the magnitude is zero; the result is the zero vector, not the scalar 0.
